key_insight: Ω-QVLA shows that vision-language-action models can be quantized more aggressively and more uniformly than previously thought, including the diffusion-based action head. By combining composite rotation with per-step scaling, it makes low-bit deployment far more stable and practical.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the high memory and compute cost of deploying large VLA models on-device, especially the challenge of quantizing diffusion-based action heads without causing instability or major accuracy loss.
method: Applies composite rotation to improve weight/activation quantization behavior across the VLA pipeline.
Uses per-step scaling to adapt quantization dynamically for diffusion action generation steps.
Enables more uniform quantization of both the LLM backbone and the DiT action head, reducing the need for mixed-precision exceptions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means lower deployment cost and smaller model footprints without sacrificing much performance. It opens a path toward practical on-device robot and embodied AI systems that were previously too expensive to run efficiently.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline diagram showing full-precision vs Ω-QVLA quantized VLA architecture

Bar chart showing stability improvements for uniform quantization of the DiT head
paper_title: Ω-QVLA: Robust Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models via Composite Rotation and Per-step Scaling
paper_authors: Xinyu Wang, Mingze Li, Sicheng Lyu, Dongxiu Liu, Kaicheng Yang
